answer: The lagoon graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the crystal audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 89 keys loses far more than 89 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the tide checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
